items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: I like the ones when he had people like Eddie Miller and George Brunis and Pee Wee Russell with him.

ctx.x: Joe Shallon at 103 Royal. S-H-A-L-O-N. You can try him, because those records are rare, and they're hard to get. But even the reissues become collector's items in a very short time. Okay, thank you very much.

Okay, we thank you for calling. Let's talk it over. Gentlemen, what about another New Orleans musician? What about Louis Prima? Any comments? Dick Allen. I haven't heard much from Louis Prima lately. Of course, I collect old records, and I like the ones when he had people like Eddie Miller and George Brunis and Pee Wee Russell with him. Those happen to be my favorites. And some with, well, what do you call them? Monk Meyer? Gene Meyer?

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: I was going to use Snoozer Quinn on guitar and Siegfried Christensen on piano and Eddie Miller on clarinet and I was going to play cornet

ctx.x: I don't know what Celestine was doing. It was Schatz for a while. It was Schatz Madison.

I don't know, but one of them was a mean man and the other one was, one trumpet player was a mean guy and the other one was a very nice fellow. Well, I set them to rehearsing across, Wailines had a sort of a warehouse across the street and without getting any permission because I knew I couldn't get permission for this, I just took it upon myself to take them over there. The Victor recording people were coming down pretty soon and I was trying to rehearse them for a date with the Victor people. and I just took…
